children: NSE shares advance in 14 of the 18 trading sessions so far in November, following a rally of around 34 per cent in October

Shares of the National Stock Exchange (NSE) extended their rally on Thursday, November 26, pushing the exchange operator’s market capitalisation close to Rs 6 lakh crore and making it the world’s third-largest listed exchange by market value. The stock touched a fresh post-listing high of Rs 2,400, overtaking Deutsche Boerse and the London Stock Exchange in the global valuation rankings.

At a market value of around USD 64.1 billion, NSE moved ahead of Deutsche Boerse, valued at USD 63.4 billion, and the London Stock Exchange at USD 62.4 billion. It now trails only CME Group, with a market capitalisation of USD 111.6 billion, and Intercontinental Exchange, valued at USD 99.4 billion.

The latest gains extend a strong run for the newly listed stock. NSE shares have advanced in 14 of the 18 trading sessions so far in November, following a rally of around 34 per cent in October. The stock has recovered nearly 50 per cent from its post-listing low of Rs 1,640, which was below its IPO price of Rs 1,785.

NSE made its stock market debut on September 24, 2026, at Rs 1,800 per share, a modest premium over the issue price. On Thursday, the shares were trading around Rs 2,375, up 2.5 per cent, after retreating from the day’s record high. The stock is now about 33 per cent above its IPO price.

The rally comes even as HSBC initiated coverage on NSE with a ‘Hold’ rating and a price target of Rs 2,300 on Thursday. The brokerage acknowledged the exchange’s strong franchise but said its current valuation already reflects much of its strengths.
HSBC’s call marks the first neutral recommendation among analysts tracking the stock. Until Thursday, all 17 analysts covering NSE had a ‘Buy’ rating.
Earlier this week, ICICI Securities set the highest price target on the Street at Rs 2,650, adding to the positive analyst outlook on the stock.
